description: The bank wants a BVN, the phone company a NIN, the state a certificate of indigeneship, the employer a birth certificate. Each enrolment needs documents the others issue.
energy_note: A circle of systems, each demanding the others.

aspect: Enrolment is a day, or several
description: Queues at enrolment centres, systems offline, biometrics failing, forms reprinted. The cost is not the fee; it is the working days.
energy_note: Three days off work to obtain a number.

description: A name change on marriage must be propagated across every registry separately, and any registry not updated produces a mismatch that is treated as the woman's error.
energy_note: Married, and now inconsistent across six databases.

aspect: Certificate of indigeneship follows the husband, not the woman
description: Indigeneship is tied to origin, and a married woman is frequently treated as an indigene of neither her birth state nor her husband's - one of the specific gaps the 2022 gender bills tried to close and failed.
energy_note: From nowhere, officially, once you marry.

description: She arrives at six to be forty-first in the queue. The system is down until eleven. At two the operator says the fingerprint scanner will not read her right thumb - she has traded dried fish for nine years - and she should come back with a letter.
energy_note: Biometrics that cannot read a working hand.
